methodology: Bounded preliminary screening; compared open PR #272 (7:136–140) and issue/PR #93 RLS warning. Primary critical editions and manuscript witnesses have not been collated; source references below are research leads only, not verified/public associations. No borrowing claim.

records.topic: Deliverance from Pharaoh's people; killing sons and sparing women
records.notes: Both traditions describe oppression of Israelites and divine deliverance; Exodus describes a decree against male infants, while this Qur'anic verse retrospectively frames the ordeal as a trial.
records.pending_question: Check the Hebrew wording of Pharaoh's order and whether Quranic 'women' means daughters; compare with 2:49 and 14:6.

records.topic: Moses appointed for thirty nights completed by ten; Aaron left in charge
records.notes: The mountain meeting and forty-day period are comparable, but Exodus 24:18 describes forty days and nights without a thirty-plus-ten division; Aaron's delegated role differs.
records.pending_question: Check MT/LXX chronology and Aaron's instructions; distinguish 40 days from Quranic 30+10 nights.

records.topic: Moses asks to see God; mountain manifestation and collapse
records.notes: Moses' request for a divine manifestation and the limit of human perception provide a strong episode-level comparison; the Qur'an describes the mountain crumbling and Moses falling unconscious, unlike the Exodus cleft-of-rock scene.
records.pending_question: Collate MT/LXX on seeing glory/face, identify differences in theophany and mountain imagery, check pre-Islamic exegetical witnesses.

records.topic: God chooses Moses for messages and speaking; instruction to give thanks
records.notes: Moses' distinctive direct communication with God is a shared motif; neither selected Exodus text has the exact Qur'anic speech of election and gratitude.
records.pending_question: Check Hebrew speech terminology and any early Jewish or Syriac retelling with closer phrasing.

records.topic: Tablets inscribed with exhortation and explanation; command to hold fast
records.notes: Both accounts describe divinely written tablets given to Moses; Exodus emphasizes tablets of testimony and the divine writing, whereas Qur'an 7:145 describes admonition and exposition and warns of the fate of transgressors.
records.pending_question: Collate tablet inscriptions and scope of contents in MT/LXX; check 7:150–154 and biblical narrative order.

pending_questions: Independently compare the indicated Hebrew Bible passages in named Masoretic and Septuagint editions; distinguish composition from extant manuscript dates.
Investigate earlier Jewish, Christian and Syriac commentary on Moses' vision and the tablets without assuming dependence.
Reconcile unmerged screening PRs into an authoritative unique-key coverage ledger.
Audit public.ancient_sources SELECT/RLS before promoting any staged row.
